{"id":"AI-707","uuid":"18e82a8a-29f8-4192-970b-637f79cb3c92","title":"Spec: marimo semantic-search notebook app for CMU lectures (molab + LanceDB Cloud)","description":"Copied from [https://github.com/elviskahoro/epic-sermons/issues/1](<https://github.com/elviskahoro/epic-sermons/issues/1>) (closed there; this is now the source of truth).

## Summary

Build a **public marimo notebook app on molab** that lets anyone run semantic + keyword search over the **CMU Database Group lecture transcripts**. Vectors live in **LanceDB Cloud**. Each query is embedded inside the notebook with **Nomic embed v1.5 (768 dimensions) on the molab CPU**, so viewers need no key and no GPU. Results are *moments in a lecture*, each linking to the exact timestamp on YouTube.

Related Linear issues: <issue id="9656209c-afac-44a9-807b-6039223bace0" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-702/transcribe-the-595-cmu-mp3s-with-whisper-large-v3-on-modal">AI-702</issue> (transcribe), <issue id="b18214c6-ac48-4a0b-b991-8a625df4b547" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-703/decide-on-the-embedding-model-openai-vs-sentence-transformers-on-molab">AI-703</issue> (embedding model), <issue id="2d9cf831-9997-4b73-b9da-bedde5ab1d79" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-704/embed-transcripts-and-load-them-into-lancedb-cloud">AI-704</issue> (load LanceDB), <issue id="e6cdd2f3-cce6-4424-abfa-b34c33c0fcce" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-705/build-the-marimo-search-notebook">AI-705</issue> (notebook), <issue id="f69f646e-c6a0-48a0-9cd7-c43935b08fbd" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-706/commit-downloadpy-changes-and-gitignore-update-in-epic-sermons">AI-706</issue> (commit download changes).

> **Spec status:** v2, updated after a walkthrough on 2026-11-01; decision 9 amended after the prompt pilot. The "Decision log" lists every choice made; "Open items" lists what is still unverified.

## Decision log

| \# | Topic | Decision |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Corpus | CMU lectures only. Emails are a **separate future project** (own issue, smaller model). |
| 2 | Audience | **Public**, anyone with the link, no login. Hosted on **molab** (must stay on molab). |
| 3 | Model | **Nomic embed v1.5**, **768 dimensions**. A bigger model (Qwen3-8B) was considered and rejected for v1. |
| 4 | Query embedding | **Local on the molab CPU**, using the same weights as the model card; no viewer key, no GPU needed. |
| 5 | Chunking | **Required.** About **60-90 s windows with \~15 s overlap**, built from Whisper segments. |
| 6 | Result unit | A **moment in a lecture**: snippet, lecture title and date, timestamped YouTube link, similarity score. |
| 7 | Corpus embedding | **Fireworks serverless** (`nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`). Gated by a parity test; if it fails, **re-embed locally on the molab GPU**. |
| 8 | Controls | Top-k selector, date-range filter, lecture filter, and **hybrid keyword + vector search with a weight slider**. |
| 9 | Transcription | Existing Whisper Large V3 pipeline on Modal, **without a vocabulary prompt**. A prompt pilot gave no gain on product names and caused a repetition loop and dropped text in one test, so the approach was dropped. |
| 10 | LanceDB key | **Read-only key** if LanceDB supports one; otherwise this table lives in its **own LanceDB project**. |
| 11 | Quality bar | **10 realistic queries, expected lecture in the top 10**, informal check before publishing. |
| 12 | Updates | **Out of scope**: the corpus is frozen at the current 595 videos. |
| 13 | No-GPU fallback | **Run on CPU.** Nomic is small, so this is the default path, not a fallback. |

## Current state

* 595 videos from the channel's Videos tab (Shorts excluded) are downloaded as 320 kbps MP3s, with per-video `.kson` metadata and `.webp` thumbnails (`src/youtube/download.py`).
* All 1,787 files are in R2 bucket `epic-sermons-raw` under `CMUDatabaseGroup/` (per-video files in `assets/`).
* Filenames follow `YYYY-MM-DD·<video_id>.<ext>`, so every record traces back to its YouTube video.
* **Not done yet:** transcription, chunking, embedding, LanceDB loading, and the notebook.

## Goals

1. A public notebook app where a user types a natural-language query and gets ranked results with links to the exact moment in the video.
2. Zero setup for viewers: no API key, no GPU, no installs.
3. Query embedding runs inside the notebook with the same model that embedded the corpus.
4. Cheap to run and reproducible from the notebook file (pinned dependencies).

## Non-goals

* Emails or any other corpus (separate issue later).
* Ingesting new videos after launch (corpus is frozen at 595).
* Transcription or embedding UI inside the notebook (offline steps).
* Accounts, history, or write access.
* Answer generation (RAG); search results only.

## Architecture

```
offline pipeline (owner)                         molab notebook app (public)
------------------------                         ---------------------------
MP3s (R2) -> Whisper (Modal)      query text (+ filters, slider)
  -> transcripts -> chunk (60-90 s, 15 s overlap)        |
  -> embed w/ "search_document: " (Fireworks)            v
          |                                      embed_query(): local Nomic, CPU
          v                                       "search_query: " prefix
     LanceDB Cloud  <----------------------------- hybrid search (vector + keyword)
                                                         |
                                                         v
                                           results table + YouTube timestamp links
```

* LanceDB Cloud does **not** embed queries server-side, so the notebook produces the query vector and passes it to `search`.
* Corpus and query vectors must use the **same model, dimension, and prefix convention**.

## Embedding model

`nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`**, 768 dimensions.**

| Property | Value |
| -- | -- |
| Dimensions | 768 (native size; no truncation) |
| Max input | 8192 tokens (chunks are far smaller) |
| Corpus embedding | Fireworks serverless, model id `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5` |
| Query embedding | Local `sentence-transformers` on the molab CPU |
| Prefixes | `search_document: ` for chunks, `search_query: ` for queries |
| Loading | Per the model card, `trust_remote_code` is not needed from `transformers` 5.5.0 and `sentence-transformers` 5.3.0 |

**Parity gate (must pass before loading the full corpus):** embed 20+ sample chunks through Fireworks and through the local model; cosine similarity between the two vectors for the same text must be **at least 0.99** (proposed threshold). If it fails, re-embed the corpus locally on the molab GPU (same code path as queries). Also confirm how Fireworks handles the prefix (it has a `prompt_template` field) so documents are not prefixed twice or not at all.

**Considered and rejected for v1:** Qwen3-Embedding-8B (heavier: \~16 GB of weights by my estimate, needs the GPU or API calls at query time), `bge-base-en-v1.5` and `gte-base` (512-token limit), 1024-dimension models, 384 dimensions.

## Data model (LanceDB table)

| Column | Type | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `id` | string | `<video_id>:<chunk_index>` |
| `video_id` | string | 11-character YouTube id |
| `date` | date | from the filename |
| `title` | string | from the `.kson` metadata |
| `chunk_index` | int | position within the lecture |
| `start_seconds` / `end_seconds` | float | from the Whisper segments |
| `text` | string | chunk text, **without** the prefix; full-text indexed for hybrid search |
| `vector` | fixed_size_list<float32>\[768\] |  |

Deep link: `https://youtu.be/<video_id>?t=<int(start_seconds)>`.

Size estimate: about 40,000 chunks (595 lectures x \~90 min / \~75 s windows, my estimate) x 768 floats ≈ 120 MB of vectors.

## Notebook UX

1. Title, short description, and a line on what the corpus covers.
2. Search form (`mo.ui.form` around a text area) so embedding runs only on submit.
3. Controls: **top-k** (default 10, max 50), **date range**, **lecture filter** (multi-select), and a **keyword-vs-semantic weight slider** (hybrid search).
4. Results in `mo.ui.table`, one row per moment: **snippet**, **lecture title and date**, **clickable timestamped YouTube link**, **similarity score**.
5. Loading state (the model loads on the first query after a cold start), empty state, and friendly errors for missing configuration or an unreachable database.
6. Footer: model id and dimension, corpus size, "corpus frozen at 595 lectures".

## Code structure

* Pinned inline dependencies (PEP 723 header): `marimo`, `lancedb`, `sentence-transformers>=5.3`.
* `load_model(model_id)` under `mo.cache` (once per kernel); device is `cuda` if available, else `cpu`.
* `embed_query(query, model_id)` under `mo.persistent_cache`; the key includes the model id.
* `mo.stop(...)` guards for missing configuration.
* Hybrid search: vector + full-text query combined with the slider weight.

## Configuration and secrets

| Variable | Purpose |
| -- | -- |
| `LANCEDB_URI` | LanceDB Cloud database for this table |
| `LANCEDB_API_KEY` | **Read-only** key if available; otherwise a key scoped to a dedicated project containing only this table |

Rules:

* Set values in the molab secrets pane (writes `.env`). Never put secrets in the notebook source.
* Treat the notebook source as public if its link is shared. **Share the app URL ("Run as app"), not the notebook URL.**
* Do not use third-party widgets that keep secrets in widget state.
* No Fireworks key in the public app (only the offline pipeline uses it).

## Deployment on molab

* Run as app on the default compute (4 CPUs, 32 GB RAM). Sessions last up to 12 hours; idle notebooks stop after 90 minutes.
* Model weights are **not persisted** between sessions, so Nomic (\~0.5 GB, estimate) re-downloads on each cold start. Show a loading message.
* Possible one kernel per browser tab (documented for self-hosted marimohub; unconfirmed for molab). Nomic is small, but test memory with several concurrent tabs.
* Molab is free "as long as usage is reasonable"; limits may change.

## Offline pipeline

1. Transcribe all 595 MP3s with Whisper Large V3 on Modal (`src/youtube/transcribe.py`) **without** a vocabulary prompt (dropped after the pilot; the optional `--prompt` flag stays in the script but is not used).
2. Chunk into 60-90 s windows with \~15 s overlap, carrying `start_seconds` and metadata.
3. Run the **parity gate**, then embed chunks with `search_document: ` prefixes via Fireworks and write to LanceDB Cloud.
4. Create a full-text index on `text` (and a vector index if latency needs it).

## Testing and verification

* **Parity gate** (above).
* **Transcript spot-check:** read 3-5 transcripts for jargon errors before the full embedding run.
* **Retrieval check:** 10 realistic queries; the expected lecture must appear in the top 10 results. Record results for vector-only vs hybrid at a few slider settings.
* **Concurrency check:** open several tabs on the published app and watch memory and latency.
* **Cold-start check:** time the first query after an idle shutdown.
* **Secrets check:** load the app and notebook logged out; confirm no key is visible; inspect an HTML export.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 595 lectures are transcribed, chunked, embedded, and queryable in LanceDB Cloud with the schema above.
- [ ] Parity gate passes (or the corpus has been re-embedded locally).
- [ ] The notebook runs as a public molab app with no viewer-side keys or GPU.
- [ ] Each result shows snippet, lecture title and date, a working timestamped YouTube link, and a score.
- [ ] Top-k, date-range, lecture filter, and the hybrid weight slider all work.
- [ ] 10-query retrieval check passes (expected lecture in top 10).
- [ ] Dependencies are pinned and the notebook runs from a clean molab start.
- [ ] Missing configuration produces a helpful message, not a stack trace.
- [ ] Secrets check passes.
- [ ] Short docs on how to re-embed and redeploy.

## Open items (unverified)

1. Does LanceDB Cloud offer **read-only API keys**? If not, create a dedicated project.
2. Does **LanceDB Cloud support full-text search plus a weighted hybrid combination** the way the slider needs it? Confirm before building the UI.
3. Does Fireworks give vectors **matching the local model**, and how does it treat the `search_document: ` prefix? (The parity gate answers this.)
4. ~~Can ~~`~~src/youtube/transcribe.py~~`~~ take a Whisper initial prompt?~~ **Resolved:** yes, but we are **not using one**. The pilot showed no benefit and a repetition loop with dropped text on one talk. Misspelled product names (for example YugabyteDB) remain a known limitation; consider an optional glossary post-correction if keyword search suffers.
5. Molab concurrency behavior (one kernel per tab?) and cold-start time.
6. Estimates to validate: \~18,000 tokens per lecture, \~40,000 chunks, \~120 MB of vectors, \~0.5 GB Nomic download.
7. Molab terms/limits can change; the free tier is "reasonable usage".

## Task breakdown

- [X] ~~Add a vocabulary prompt to transcription and run a pilot~~ Dropped after the pilot
- [ ] Optional: glossary post-correction for common jargon misspellings (only if keyword search needs it)
- [ ] Transcribe all 595 MP3s; spot-check
- [ ] Chunking and metadata script
- [ ] Parity gate (Fireworks vs local Nomic)
- [ ] Embed and load into LanceDB Cloud; create the full-text index
- [ ] Verify read-only key and hybrid search support
- [ ] Notebook v1: form, search, results table, links
- [ ] Controls: top-k, date range, lecture filter, hybrid slider
- [ ] Deploy as a molab app; run the concurrency, cold-start, and secrets checks
- [ ] 10-query retrieval check
- [ ] Docs

## References

* molab guide: [https://docs.marimo.io/guides/molab/](<https://docs.marimo.io/guides/molab/>)
* marimo caching API: [https://docs.marimo.io/api/caching/](<https://docs.marimo.io/api/caching/>)
* molab storage and caching post: [https://molab.marimo.io/blog/seamless-storage-in-molab](<https://molab.marimo.io/blog/seamless-storage-in-molab>)
* LanceDB embeddings: [https://docs.lancedb.com/embedding](<https://docs.lancedb.com/embedding>)
* Fireworks embeddings: [https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/querying-embeddings-models](<https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/querying-embeddings-models>)
* Nomic embed v1.5: [https://huggingface.co/nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5](<https://huggingface.co/nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5>)","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-707/spec-marimo-semantic-search-notebook-app-for-cmu-lectures-molab","gitBranchName":"feature/ai-707","createdAt":"2026-11-02T19:02:46.275Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-02T19:02:46.275Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[{"id":"b66535d3-845d-4db6-9321-794ffeb5cc86","title":"GitHub epic-sermons #1","subtitle":null,"url":"https://github.com/elviskahoro/epic-sermons/issues/1"}],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"f9ac7ea1-d17d-4e1c-a1e4-a7e2e887b660","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-11-02T19:02:46.275Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"elvis kahoro","createdById":"cef7de02-fcc2-4a6f-b787-beac2bd2440c","project":"CMU Database Group: search over lecture transcripts","projectId":"a5ddbdae-8d93-45af-98e5-346cc5c55ea0","team":"AI","teamId":"6ec292fd-c37d-41fb-9e1f-f1b15b29cf23"}

**Parity gate (must pass before loading the full corpus):** embed 20+ sample chunks through Fireworks and through the local model; cosine similarity between the two vectors for the same text must be **at least 0.99** (proposed threshold). If it fails, re-embed the corpus locally on the molab GPU (same code path as queries). Also confirm how Fireworks handles the prefix (it has a `prompt_template` field) so documents are not prefixed twice or not at all.

**Considered and rejected for v1:** Qwen3-Embedding-8B (heavier: \~16 GB of weights by my estimate, needs the GPU or API calls at query time), `bge-base-en-v1.5` and `gte-base` (512-token limit), 1024-dimension models, 384 dimensions.

## Data model (LanceDB table)

| Column | Type | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `id` | string | `<video_id>:<chunk_index>` |
| `video_id` | string | 11-character YouTube id |
| `date` | date | from the filename |
| `title` | string | from the `.kson` metadata |
| `chunk_index` | int | position within the lecture |
| `start_seconds` / `end_seconds` | float | from the Whisper segments |
| `text` | string | chunk text, **without** the prefix; full-text indexed for hybrid search |
| `vector` | fixed_size_list<float32>\[768\] |  |

Deep link: `https://youtu.be/<video_id>?t=<int(start_seconds)>`.

Size estimate: about 40,000 chunks (595 lectures x \~90 min / \~75 s windows, my estimate) x 768 floats ≈ 120 MB of vectors.

## Notebook UX

1. Title, short description, and a line on what the corpus covers.
2. Search form (`mo.ui.form` around a text area) so embedding runs only on submit.
3. Controls: **top-k** (default 10, max 50), **date range**, **lecture filter** (multi-select), and a **keyword-vs-semantic weight slider** (hybrid search).
4. Results in `mo.ui.table`, one row per moment: **snippet**, **lecture title and date**, **clickable timestamped YouTube link**, **similarity score**.
5. Loading state (the model loads on the first query after a cold start), empty state, and friendly errors for missing configuration or an unreachable database.
6. Footer: model id and dimension, corpus size, "corpus frozen at 595 lectures".

## Code structure

* Pinned inline dependencies (PEP 723 header): `marimo`, `lancedb`, `sentence-transformers>=5.3`.
* `load_model(model_id)` under `mo.cache` (once per kernel); device is `cuda` if available, else `cpu`.
* `embed_query(query, model_id)` under `mo.persistent_cache`; the key includes the model id.
* `mo.stop(...)` guards for missing configuration.
* Hybrid search: vector + full-text query combined with the slider weight.

## Configuration and secrets

| Variable | Purpose |
| -- | -- |
| `LANCEDB_URI` | LanceDB Cloud database for this table |
| `LANCEDB_API_KEY` | **Read-only** key if available; otherwise a key scoped to a dedicated project containing only this table |

Rules:

* Set values in the molab secrets pane (writes `.env`). Never put secrets in the notebook source.
* Treat the notebook source as public if its link is shared. **Share the app URL ("Run as app"), not the notebook URL.**
* Do not use third-party widgets that keep secrets in widget state.
* No Fireworks key in the public app (only the offline pipeline uses it).

## Deployment on molab

* Run as app on the default compute (4 CPUs, 32 GB RAM). Sessions last up to 12 hours; idle notebooks stop after 90 minutes.
* Model weights are **not persisted** between sessions, so Nomic (\~0.5 GB, estimate) re-downloads on each cold start. Show a loading message.
* Possible one kernel per browser tab (documented for self-hosted marimohub; unconfirmed for molab). Nomic is small, but test memory with several concurrent tabs.
* Molab is free "as long as usage is reasonable"; limits may change.

## Offline pipeline

1. Transcribe all 595 MP3s with Whisper Large V3 on Modal (`src/youtube/transcribe.py`) **without** a vocabulary prompt (dropped after the pilot; the optional `--prompt` flag stays in the script but is not used).
2. Chunk into 60-90 s windows with \~15 s overlap, carrying `start_seconds` and metadata.
3. Run the **parity gate**, then embed chunks with `search_document: ` prefixes via Fireworks and write to LanceDB Cloud.
4. Create a full-text index on `text` (and a vector index if latency needs it).

## Testing and verification

* **Parity gate** (above).
* **Transcript spot-check:** read 3-5 transcripts for jargon errors before the full embedding run.
* **Retrieval check:** 10 realistic queries; the expected lecture must appear in the top 10 results. Record results for vector-only vs hybrid at a few slider settings.
* **Concurrency check:** open several tabs on the published app and watch memory and latency.
* **Cold-start check:** time the first query after an idle shutdown.
* **Secrets check:** load the app and notebook logged out; confirm no key is visible; inspect an HTML export.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 595 lectures are transcribed, chunked, embedded, and queryable in LanceDB Cloud with the schema above.
- [ ] Parity gate passes (or the corpus has been re-embedded locally).
- [ ] The notebook runs as a public molab app with no viewer-side keys or GPU.
- [ ] Each result shows snippet, lecture title and date, a working timestamped YouTube link, and a score.
- [ ] Top-k, date-range, lecture filter, and the hybrid weight slider all work.
- [ ] 10-query retrieval check passes (expected lecture in top 10).
- [ ] Dependencies are pinned and the notebook runs from a clean molab start.
- [ ] Missing configuration produces a helpful message, not a stack trace.
- [ ] Secrets check passes.
- [ ] Short docs on how to re-embed and redeploy.

## Open items (unverified)

1. Does LanceDB Cloud offer **read-only API keys**? If not, create a dedicated project.
2. Does **LanceDB Cloud support full-text search plus a weighted hybrid combination** the way the slider needs it? Confirm before building the UI.
3. Does Fireworks give vectors **matching the local model**, and how does it treat the `search_document: ` prefix? (The parity gate answers this.)
4. ~~Can ~~`~~src/youtube/transcribe.py~~`~~ take a Whisper initial prompt?~~ **Resolved:** yes, but we are **not using one**. The pilot showed no benefit and a repetition loop with dropped text on one talk. Misspelled product names (for example YugabyteDB) remain a known limitation; consider an optional glossary post-correction if keyword search suffers.
5. Molab concurrency behavior (one kernel per tab?) and cold-start time.
6. Estimates to validate: \~18,000 tokens per lecture, \~40,000 chunks, \~120 MB of vectors, \~0.5 GB Nomic download.
7. Molab terms/limits can change; the free tier is "reasonable usage".

## Task breakdown

- [X] ~~Add a vocabulary prompt to transcription and run a pilot~~ Dropped after the pilot
- [ ] Optional: glossary post-correction for common jargon misspellings (only if keyword search needs it)
- [ ] Transcribe all 595 MP3s; spot-check
- [ ] Chunking and metadata script
- [ ] Parity gate (Fireworks vs local Nomic)
- [ ] Embed and load into LanceDB Cloud; create the full-text index
- [ ] Verify read-only key and hybrid search support
- [ ] Notebook v1: form, search, results table, links
- [ ] Controls: top-k, date range, lecture filter, hybrid slider
- [ ] Deploy as a molab app; run the concurrency, cold-start, and secrets checks
- [ ] 10-query retrieval check
- [ ] Docs

## References

* molab guide: [https://docs.marimo.io/guides/molab/](<https://docs.marimo.io/guides/molab/>)
* marimo caching API: [https://docs.marimo.io/api/caching/](<https://docs.marimo.io/api/caching/>)
* molab storage and caching post: [https://molab.marimo.io/blog/seamless-storage-in-molab](<https://molab.marimo.io/blog/seamless-storage-in-molab>)
* LanceDB embeddings: [https://docs.lancedb.com/embedding](<https://docs.lancedb.com/embedding>)
* Fireworks embeddings: [https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/querying-embeddings-models](<https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/querying-embeddings-models>)

{"id":"AI-709","uuid":"323c3d7b-0e64-4804-bd14-ec9ca030948a","title":"Handoff: CMU lecture search project - state, runbook, and roadmap","description":"Copied from [https://github.com/elviskahoro/epic-sermons/issues/3](<https://github.com/elviskahoro/epic-sermons/issues/3>) (closed there; this is now the source of truth). Repo: `/Users/elvis/Documents/hq/repos/epic-sermons`.

## Purpose

Handoff for an agent (or person) continuing the CMU Database Group lecture search project: current state, access and gotchas, guardrails, the immediate next task (full transcription) with exact commands, and the remaining roadmap. Related Linear issues: <issue id="9656209c-afac-44a9-807b-6039223bace0" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-702/transcribe-the-595-cmu-mp3s-with-whisper-large-v3-on-modal">AI-702</issue> (transcribe), <issue id="b18214c6-ac48-4a0b-b991-8a625df4b547" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-703/decide-on-the-embedding-model-openai-vs-sentence-transformers-on-molab">AI-703</issue> (embedding model), <issue id="2d9cf831-9997-4b73-b9da-bedde5ab1d79" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-704/embed-transcripts-and-load-them-into-lancedb-cloud">AI-704</issue> (load LanceDB), <issue id="e6cdd2f3-cce6-4424-abfa-b34c33c0fcce" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-705/build-the-marimo-search-notebook">AI-705</issue> (notebook), <issue id="f69f646e-c6a0-48a0-9cd7-c43935b08fbd" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-706/commit-downloadpy-changes-and-gitignore-update-in-epic-sermons">AI-706</issue> (commit download changes; the changes are committed, so this can be closed after checking).

**Goal:** a public marimo notebook app on molab doing hybrid (semantic + keyword) search over the lecture transcripts. Vectors in LanceDB Cloud, queries embedded locally with Nomic v1.5 (768 dims), results are moments in a lecture with timestamped YouTube links.

## Where we are

| Stage | Status |
| -- | -- |
| Download 595 videos as 320 kbps MP3 + `.kson` + `.webp` | **Done** (`out/CMUDatabaseGroup/assets/`, \~92 GB) |
| Upload to Cloudflare R2 (`epic-sermons-raw`, prefix `CMUDatabaseGroup/`) | **Done** (595 MP3 + 1,192 metadata/thumbnail files; success judged by wrangler exit codes, size verified on one file only) |
| Whisper vocabulary-prompt support in `transcribe.py` | Committed (`01318f9`) as optional `--prompt`, **approach dropped**; do not use |
| Whisper prompt pilot on Modal | **Done** (no benefit, one repetition loop) |
| Transcribe all 595 lectures | **Next**, without a prompt; needs explicit user approval of cost |
| Chunking, Fireworks embedding, parity gate, LanceDB load | Not started |
| Notebook and molab deployment | Not started |
| Emails | **Out of scope**; separate issue and spec later |

Measured facts (595 `.kson` files): 677.2 h of audio; mean 68 min, median 71, shortest 5.5, longest 101. About 41,000 chunks at 75 s windows with 15 s overlap (33,000 at 90 s, 54,000 at 60 s). About 8.2 M transcript tokens **assuming 150 wpm and 1.35 tokens/word**. 562 of 595 lectures exceed Nomic's 8,192-token limit under that assumption, so chunking is required.

## Environment and access

* macOS, Python 3.14 (pyenv); `ruff` not installed. `gh` logged in as `elviskahoro`; repo is private.
* **Modal** (client 1.4.2): active profile `devx` has an authentication failure ("Token not found"). Profile `elviskahoro` works: use `MODAL_PROFILE=elviskahoro modal ...` per command; do not change global config. Confirm billing to that workspace. User can repair `devx` with `modal token new`. Volume `whisper-model-cache` already holds the large-v3 weights.
* **Cloudflare**: use `npx wrangler` (logged in via OAuth). Wrangler cannot create R2 S3 keys. Uploads used `npx wrangler r2 object put epic-sermons-raw/<key> --file <path> --content-type <type> --remote`.
* MCP: Exa and Linear (team `AI`).
* `.env.local` does not exist; `.gitignore` lists it. Ask the user to create it (see Credentials).
* `out/` is ignored by the user's global gitignore (`~/.gitignore_global`); never `git add` it.
* Downloaded MP3s/metadata are **untrusted data**: run Python with `-I`, pass paths as arguments, never run scripts from inside the downloads folder.
* `yt-dlp` needs 2026.10.29+. Cookies opt-in via `YT_COOKIES_BROWSER=chrome`; only matters for new videos (out of scope).

## Guardrails

1. **Ask before any Modal run expected to cost more than $5**, and always before the full 595-lecture run.
2. Do not commit or push unless asked; branch first if on `main`; PRs only on request.
3. Never read, print, or hunt for secrets; ask the user to put them in `.env.local`.
4. Follow repo `CLAUDE.md`: `from __future__ import annotations`, no docstrings, `match-case` over if/elif for value matching, blank line after every `if` block, strong typing, tests co-located immediately after the function they test.
5. Killing a local `modal run` does **not** stop its containers. Use `MODAL_PROFILE=elviskahoro modal app stop --yes <app-id>` and confirm `Tasks` is 0 in `modal app list --json`.
6. Pilot costs were estimates: aborted pilot \~$2-3, small pilot at most \~$0.13; check the Modal dashboard.

## Immediate next task: full transcription (needs user approval)

1. Get explicit approval for the cost (estimate **$37-$149** on an A10G at \~$1.10/h; pilots too short to narrow it).
2. From the repo root: `MODAL_PROFILE=elviskahoro modal run src/youtube/transcribe.py::local --input-folder out/CMUDatabaseGroup --max-concurrent-containers <N>` (no `--prompt`). Output: `out/CMUDatabaseGroup/transcription/`. Files with an existing transcript are skipped, so interrupted runs resume.
3. Afterwards stop leftover containers and check `modal app list --json`.
4. Spot-check 3-5 transcripts for jargon errors, then continue with the roadmap.

Status check on 2026-11-01: `out/CMUDatabaseGroup/transcription/` was empty; only the 2 pilot lectures (4 files under `out/pilot2_*`) are transcribed.

## Remaining roadmap (order matters)

1. **Full transcription** of 595 MP3s (above), then spot-check.
2. **Chunking script** (new module, co-located typed tests): group Whisper segments into \~60-90 s windows with \~15 s overlap; carry `video_id`, `date`, `title`, `chunk_index`, `start_seconds`, `end_seconds`, `text`. Deep link: `https://youtu.be/<video_id>?t=<int(start_seconds)>`.
3. **Parity gate:** embed 20+ sample chunks via Fireworks (`nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`, `search_document: ` prefix) and locally with `sentence-transformers>=5.3`; cosine similarity at least 0.99 (proposed). Confirm how Fireworks treats the prefix (`prompt_template`). If it fails, re-embed locally on the molab GPU. Needs `FIREWORKS_API_KEY`. Fireworks Nomic pricing $0.008 per M input tokens (\~$0.10 for the corpus, estimate).
4. **LanceDB:** confirm which product the user has (docs call Cloud "legacy", Enterprise current), whether a read-only key is possible, run the hybrid-search check (FTS index on `text`, `query_type="hybrid"` with explicit `.vector(...).text(...)`). `LinearCombinationReranker` is deprecated; `MRRReranker(weight_vector, weight_fts)` is the weighted option for the slider. Create the table and load vectors. Needs `LANCEDB_URI` and `LANCEDB_API_KEY`.
5. **Notebook v1** (marimo, pinned PEP 723 header): form-driven search, top-k, date range, lecture filter, hybrid slider, results table with snippet, title/date, timestamped link, score. `mo.cache` for the model, `mo.persistent_cache` for query embeddings (key includes model id).
6. **Molab deployment and checks:** consider a probe notebook reporting GPU, memory, model load time, outbound network; test concurrency/memory with several tabs, cold start, secrets visibility logged out, HTML export. Share the **app URL**, not the notebook URL.
7. **Retrieval check:** 10 realistic queries (ask the user), expected lecture in the top 10; compare vector-only vs hybrid.
8. **Docs** for re-embedding and redeploying; update Linear issues <issue id="9656209c-afac-44a9-807b-6039223bace0" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-702/transcribe-the-595-cmu-mp3s-with-whisper-large-v3-on-modal">AI-702</issue> through <issue id="f69f646e-c6a0-48a0-9cd7-c43935b08fbd" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-706/commit-downloadpy-changes-and-gitignore-update-in-epic-sermons">AI-706</issue>.

### Credentials

Do not search for them. Ask the user to create `.env.local` (git-ignored) with `FIREWORKS_API_KEY`, `LANCEDB_URI`, `LANCEDB_API_KEY`. Molab secrets are set separately through the molab secrets pane.

## Known gotchas

* Optional `--prompt` flag exists (prompts over 40 tokens rejected) but is **not used**.
* `transcribe.py` must be run from the repo root (uses `Path.cwd()` and imports from `src`); input files must live under the working directory.
* The transcription output directory comes from the first `out/<name>/` in the path, so pilot folders become their own "authors".
* `pytest` collects tests from every `.py` file; run `python -m pytest src/youtube/transcribe.py -q` for just this file.
* Run `modal token new` once interactively to repair the `devx` profile.
* Spec numbers marked "estimate" were computed from durations plus assumptions; recompute once transcripts exist.

## Definition of done for this handoff

- [X] Whisper prompt pilot run, evaluated, approach dropped
- [ ] Spec open items updated with verified findings
- [ ] User approves (or declines) the full transcription run and its cost
- [ ] Roadmap steps 1-8 tracked as separate issues or checklist items, each with an owner and any credentials they need
- [ ] Linear issues <issue id="9656209c-afac-44a9-807b-6039223bace0" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-702/transcribe-the-595-cmu-mp3s-with-whisper-large-v3-on-modal">AI-702</issue> through <issue id="f69f646e-c6a0-48a0-9cd7-c43935b08fbd" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-706/commit-downloadpy-changes-and-gitignore-update-in-epic-sermons">AI-706</issue> updated to match reality","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-709/handoff-cmu-lecture-search-project-state-runbook-and-roadmap","gitBranchName":"feature/ai-709","createdAt":"2026-11-02T19:03:15.161Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-02T19:03:15.161Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[{"id":"bf0ada0f-b236-4efd-ab1f-550885ac1094","title":"GitHub epic-sermons #3","subtitle":null,"url":"https://github.com/elviskahoro/epic-sermons/issues/3"}],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"f9ac7ea1-d17d-4e1c-a1e4-a7e2e887b660","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-11-02T19:03:15.161Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"elvis kahoro","createdById":"cef7de02-fcc2-4a6f-b787-beac2bd2440c","project":"CMU Database Group: search over lecture transcripts","projectId":"a5ddbdae-8d93-45af-98e5-346cc5c55ea0","team":"AI","teamId":"6ec292fd-c37d-41fb-9e1f-f1b15b29cf23"}

4. Follow repo `CLAUDE.md`: `from __future__ import annotations`, no docstrings, `match-case` over if/elif for value matching, blank line after every `if` block, strong typing, tests co-located immediately after the function they test.
5. Killing a local `modal run` does **not** stop its containers. Use `MODAL_PROFILE=elviskahoro modal app stop --yes <app-id>` and confirm `Tasks` is 0 in `modal app list --json`.
6. Pilot costs were estimates: aborted pilot \~$2-3, small pilot at most \~$0.13; check the Modal dashboard.

## Immediate next task: full transcription (needs user approval)

1. Get explicit approval for the cost (estimate **$37-$149** on an A10G at \~$1.10/h; pilots too short to narrow it).
2. From the repo root: `MODAL_PROFILE=elviskahoro modal run src/youtube/transcribe.py::local --input-folder out/CMUDatabaseGroup --max-concurrent-containers <N>` (no `--prompt`). Output: `out/CMUDatabaseGroup/transcription/`. Files with an existing transcript are skipped, so interrupted runs resume.
3. Afterwards stop leftover containers and check `modal app list --json`.
4. Spot-check 3-5 transcripts for jargon errors, then continue with the roadmap.

Status check on 2026-11-01: `out/CMUDatabaseGroup/transcription/` was empty; only the 2 pilot lectures (4 files under `out/pilot2_*`) are transcribed.

## Remaining roadmap (order matters)

1. **Full transcription** of 595 MP3s (above), then spot-check.
2. **Chunking script** (new module, co-located typed tests): group Whisper segments into \~60-90 s windows with \~15 s overlap; carry `video_id`, `date`, `title`, `chunk_index`, `start_seconds`, `end_seconds`, `text`. Deep link: `https://youtu.be/<video_id>?t=<int(start_seconds)>`.
3. **Parity gate:** embed 20+ sample chunks via Fireworks (`nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`, `search_document: ` prefix) and locally with `sentence-transformers>=5.3`; cosine similarity at least 0.99 (proposed). Confirm how Fireworks treats the prefix (`prompt_template`). If it fails, re-embed locally on the molab GPU. Needs `FIREWORKS_API_KEY`. Fireworks Nomic pricing $0.008 per M input tokens (\~$0.10 for the corpus, estimate).
4. **LanceDB:** confirm which product the user has (docs call Cloud "legacy", Enterprise current), whether a read-only key is possible, run the hybrid-search check (FTS index on `text`, `query_type="hybrid"` with explicit `.vector(...).text(...)`). `LinearCombinationReranker` is deprecated; `MRRReranker(weight_vector, weight_fts)` is the weighted option for the slider. Create the table and load vectors. Needs `LANCEDB_URI` and `LANCEDB_API_KEY`.
5. **Notebook v1** (marimo, pinned PEP 723 header): form-driven search, top-k, date range, lecture filter, hybrid slider, results table with snippet, title/date, timestamped link, score. `mo.cache` for the model, `mo.persistent_cache` for query embeddings (key includes model id).
6. **Molab deployment and checks:** consider a probe notebook reporting GPU, memory, model load time, outbound network; test concurrency/memory with several tabs, cold start, secrets visibility logged out, HTML export. Share the **app URL**, not the notebook URL.
7. **Retrieval check:** 10 realistic queries (ask the user), expected lecture in the top 10; compare vector-only vs hybrid.
8. **Docs** for re-embedding and redeploying; update Linear issues <issue id="9656209c-afac-44a9-807b-6039223bace0" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-702/transcribe-the-595-cmu-mp3s-with-whisper-large-v3-on-modal">AI-702</issue> through <issue id="f69f646e-c6a0-48a0-9cd7-c43935b08fbd" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-706/commit-downloadpy-changes-and-gitignore-update-in-epic-sermons">AI-706</issue>.

### Credentials

Do not search for them. Ask the user to create `.env.local` (git-ignored) with `FIREWORKS_API_KEY`, `LANCEDB_URI`, `LANCEDB_API_KEY`. Molab secrets are set separately through the molab secrets pane.

## Known gotchas

* Optional `--prompt` flag exists (prompts over 40 tokens rejected) but is **not used**.
* `transcribe.py` must be run from the repo root (uses `Path.cwd()` and imports from `src`); input files must live under the working directory.
* The transcription output directory comes from the first `out/<name>/` in the path, so pilot folders become their own "authors".
* `pytest` collects tests from every `.py` file; run `python -m pytest src/youtube/transcribe.py -q` for just this file.
* Run `modal token new` once interactively to repair the `devx` profile.
* Spec numbers marked "estimate" were computed from durations plus assumptions; recompute once transcripts exist.

## Definition of done for this handoff

- [X] Whisper prompt pilot run, evaluated, approach dropped
- [ ] Spec open items updated with verified findings
- [ ] User approves (or declines) the full transcription run and its cost
- [ ] Roadmap steps 1-8 tracked as separate issues or checklist items, each with an owner and any credentials they need

{"id":"AI-707","uuid":"18e82a8a-29f8-4192-970b-637f79cb3c92","title":"Spec: marimo semantic-search notebook app for CMU lectures (molab + LanceDB Cloud)","description":"Copied from [https://github.com/elviskahoro/epic-sermons/issues/1](<https://github.com/elviskahoro/epic-sermons/issues/1>) (closed there; this is now the source of truth).

## Summary

Build a **public marimo notebook app on molab** that lets anyone run semantic + keyword search over the **CMU Database Group lecture transcripts**. Vectors live in **LanceDB Cloud**. Each query is embedded inside the notebook with **Nomic embed v1.5 (768 dimensions) on the molab CPU**, so viewers need no key and no GPU. Results are *moments in a lecture*, each linking to the exact timestamp on YouTube.

Related Linear issues: <issue id="9656209c-afac-44a9-807b-6039223bace0" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-702/transcribe-the-595-cmu-mp3s-with-whisper-large-v3-on-modal">AI-702</issue> (transcribe), <issue id="b18214c6-ac48-4a0b-b991-8a625df4b547" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-703/decide-on-the-embedding-model-openai-vs-sentence-transformers-on-molab">AI-703</issue> (embedding model), <issue id="2d9cf831-9997-4b73-b9da-bedde5ab1d79" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-704/embed-transcripts-and-load-them-into-lancedb-cloud">AI-704</issue> (load LanceDB), <issue id="e6cdd2f3-cce6-4424-abfa-b34c33c0fcce" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-705/build-the-marimo-search-notebook">AI-705</issue> (notebook), <issue id="f69f646e-c6a0-48a0-9cd7-c43935b08fbd" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-706/commit-downloadpy-changes-and-gitignore-update-in-epic-sermons">AI-706</issue> (commit download changes).

> **Spec status:** v2, updated after a walkthrough on 2026-11-01; decision 9 amended after the prompt pilot. The "Decision log" lists every choice made; "Open items" lists what is still unverified.

## Decision log

| \# | Topic | Decision |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Corpus | CMU lectures only. Emails are a **separate future project** (own issue, smaller model). |
| 2 | Audience | **Public**, anyone with the link, no login. Hosted on **molab** (must stay on molab). |
| 3 | Model | **Nomic embed v1.5**, **768 dimensions**. A bigger model (Qwen3-8B) was considered and rejected for v1. |
| 4 | Query embedding | **Local on the molab CPU**, using the same weights as the model card; no viewer key, no GPU needed. |
| 5 | Chunking | **Required.** About **60-90 s windows with \~15 s overlap**, built from Whisper segments. |
| 6 | Result unit | A **moment in a lecture**: snippet, lecture title and date, timestamped YouTube link, similarity score. |
| 7 | Corpus embedding | **Fireworks serverless** (`nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`). Gated by a parity test; if it fails, **re-embed locally on the molab GPU**. |
| 8 | Controls | Top-k selector, date-range filter, lecture filter, and **hybrid keyword + vector search with a weight slider**. |
| 9 | Transcription | Existing Whisper Large V3 pipeline on Modal, **without a vocabulary prompt**. A prompt pilot gave no gain on product names and caused a repetition loop and dropped text in one test, so the approach was dropped. |
| 10 | LanceDB key | **Read-only key** if LanceDB supports one; otherwise this table lives in its **own LanceDB project**. |
| 11 | Quality bar | **10 realistic queries, expected lecture in the top 10**, informal check before publishing. |
| 12 | Updates | **Out of scope**: the corpus is frozen at the current 595 videos. |
| 13 | No-GPU fallback | **Run on CPU.** Nomic is small, so this is the default path, not a fallback. |

## Current state

* 595 videos from the channel's Videos tab (Shorts excluded) are downloaded as 320 kbps MP3s, with per-video `.kson` metadata and `.webp` thumbnails (`src/youtube/download.py`).
* All 1,787 files are in R2 bucket `epic-sermons-raw` under `CMUDatabaseGroup/` (per-video files in `assets/`).
* Filenames follow `YYYY-MM-DD·<video_id>.<ext>`, so every record traces back to its YouTube video.
* **Not done yet:** transcription, chunking, embedding, LanceDB loading, and the notebook.

## Goals

1. A public notebook app where a user types a natural-language query and gets ranked results with links to the exact moment in the video.
2. Zero setup for viewers: no API key, no GPU, no installs.
3. Query embedding runs inside the notebook with the same model that embedded the corpus.
4. Cheap to run and reproducible from the notebook file (pinned dependencies).

## Non-goals

* Emails or any other corpus (separate issue later).
* Ingesting new videos after launch (corpus is frozen at 595).
* Transcription or embedding UI inside the notebook (offline steps).
* Accounts, history, or write access.
* Answer generation (RAG); search results only.

## Architecture

```
offline pipeline (owner)                         molab notebook app (public)
------------------------                         ---------------------------
MP3s (R2) -> Whisper (Modal)      query text (+ filters, slider)
  -> transcripts -> chunk (60-90 s, 15 s overlap)        |
  -> embed w/ "search_document: " (Fireworks)            v
          |                                      embed_query(): local Nomic, CPU
          v                                       "search_query: " prefix
     LanceDB Cloud  <----------------------------- hybrid search (vector + keyword)
                                                         |
                                                         v
                                           results table + YouTube timestamp links
```

* LanceDB Cloud does **not** embed queries server-side, so the notebook produces the query vector and passes it to `search`.
* Corpus and query vectors must use the **same model, dimension, and prefix convention**.

## Embedding model

`nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`**, 768 dimensions.**

| Property | Value |
| -- | -- |
| Dimensions | 768 (native size; no truncation) |
| Max input | 8192 tokens (chunks are far smaller) |
| Corpus embedding | Fireworks serverless, model id `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5` |
| Query embedding | Local `sentence-transformers` on the molab CPU |
| Prefixes | `search_document: ` for chunks, `search_query: ` for queries |
| Loading | Per the model card, `trust_remote_code` is not needed from `transformers` 5.5.0 and `sentence-transformers` 5.3.0 |

**Parity gate (must pass before loading the full corpus):** embed 20+ sample chunks through Fireworks and through the local model; cosine similarity between the two vectors for the same text must be **at least 0.99** (proposed threshold). If it fails, re-embed the corpus locally on the molab GPU (same code path as queries). Also confirm how Fireworks handles the prefix (it has a `prompt_template` field) so documents are not prefixed twice or not at all.

**Considered and rejected for v1:** Qwen3-Embedding-8B (heavier: \~16 GB of weights by my estimate, needs the GPU or API calls at query time), `bge-base-en-v1.5` and `gte-base` (512-token limit), 1024-dimension models, 384 dimensions.

## Data model (LanceDB table)

| Column | Type | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `id` | string | `<video_id>:<chunk_index>` |
| `video_id` | string | 11-character YouTube id |
| `date` | date | from the filename |
| `title` | string | from the `.kson` metadata |
| `chunk_index` | int | position within the lecture |
| `start_seconds` / `end_seconds` | float | from the Whisper segments |
| `text` | string | chunk text, **without** the prefix; full-text indexed for hybrid search |
| `vector` | fixed_size_list<float32>\[768\] |  |

Deep link: `https://youtu.be/<video_id>?t=<int(start_seconds)>`.

Size estimate: about 40,000 chunks (595 lectures x \~90 min / \~75 s windows, my estimate) x 768 floats ≈ 120 MB of vectors.

## Notebook UX

1. Title, short description, and a line on what the corpus covers.
2. Search form (`mo.ui.form` around a text area) so embedding runs only on submit.
3. Controls: **top-k** (default 10, max 50), **date range**, **lecture filter** (multi-select), and a **keyword-vs-semantic weight slider** (hybrid search).
4. Results in `mo.ui.table`, one row per moment: **snippet**, **lecture title and date**, **clickable timestamped YouTube link**, **similarity score**.
5. Loading state (the model loads on the first query after a cold start), empty state, and friendly errors for missing configuration or an unreachable database.
6. Footer: model id and dimension, corpus size, "corpus frozen at 595 lectures".

## Code structure

* Pinned inline dependencies (PEP 723 header): `marimo`, `lancedb`, `sentence-transformers>=5.3`.
* `load_model(model_id)` under `mo.cache` (once per kernel); device is `cuda` if available, else `cpu`.
* `embed_query(query, model_id)` under `mo.persistent_cache`; the key includes the model id.
* `mo.stop(...)` guards for missing configuration.
* Hybrid search: vector + full-text query combined with the slider weight.

## Configuration and secrets

| Variable | Purpose |
| -- | -- |
| `LANCEDB_URI` | LanceDB Cloud database for this table |
| `LANCEDB_API_KEY` | **Read-only** key if available; otherwise a key scoped to a dedicated project containing only this table |

Rules:

* Set values in the molab secrets pane (writes `.env`). Never put secrets in the notebook source.
* Treat the notebook source as public if its link is shared. **Share the app URL ("Run as app"), not the notebook URL.**
* Do not use third-party widgets that keep secrets in widget state.
* No Fireworks key in the public app (only the offline pipeline uses it).

## Deployment on molab

* Run as app on the default compute (4 CPUs, 32 GB RAM). Sessions last up to 12 hours; idle notebooks stop after 90 minutes.
* Model weights are **not persisted** between sessions, so Nomic (\~0.5 GB, estimate) re-downloads on each cold start. Show a loading message.
* Possible one kernel per browser tab (documented for self-hosted marimohub; unconfirmed for molab). Nomic is small, but test memory with several concurrent tabs.
* Molab is free "as long as usage is reasonable"; limits may change.

## Offline pipeline

1. Transcribe all 595 MP3s with Whisper Large V3 on Modal (`src/youtube/transcribe.py`) **without** a vocabulary prompt (dropped after the pilot; the optional `--prompt` flag stays in the script but is not used).
2. Chunk into 60-90 s windows with \~15 s overlap, carrying `start_seconds` and metadata.
3. Run the **parity gate**, then embed chunks with `search_document: ` prefixes via Fireworks and write to LanceDB Cloud.
4. Create a full-text index on `text` (and a vector index if latency needs it).

## Testing and verification

* **Parity gate** (above).
* **Transcript spot-check:** read 3-5 transcripts for jargon errors before the full embedding run.
* **Retrieval check:** 10 realistic queries; the expected lecture must appear in the top 10 results. Record results for vector-only vs hybrid at a few slider settings.
* **Concurrency check:** open several tabs on the published app and watch memory and latency.
* **Cold-start check:** time the first query after an idle shutdown.
* **Secrets check:** load the app and notebook logged out; confirm no key is visible; inspect an HTML export.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 595 lectures are transcribed, chunked, embedded, and queryable in LanceDB Cloud with the schema above.
- [ ] Parity gate passes (or the corpus has been re-embedded locally).
- [ ] The notebook runs as a public molab app with no viewer-side keys or GPU.
- [ ] Each result shows snippet, lecture title and date, a working timestamped YouTube link, and a score.
- [ ] Top-k, date-range, lecture filter, and the hybrid weight slider all work.
- [ ] 10-query retrieval check passes (expected lecture in top 10).
- [ ] Dependencies are pinned and the notebook runs from a clean molab start.
- [ ] Missing configuration produces a helpful message, not a stack trace.
- [ ] Secrets check passes.
- [ ] Short docs on how to re-embed and redeploy.

## Open items (unverified)

1. Does LanceDB Cloud offer **read-only API keys**? If not, create a dedicated project.
2. Does **LanceDB Cloud support full-text search plus a weighted hybrid combination** the way the slider needs it? Confirm before building the UI.
3. Does Fireworks give vectors **matching the local model**, and how does it treat the `search_document: ` prefix? (The parity gate answers this.)
4. ~~Can ~~`~~src/youtube/transcribe.py~~`~~ take a Whisper initial prompt?~~ **Resolved:** yes, but we are **not using one**. The pilot showed no benefit and a repetition loop with dropped text on one talk. Misspelled product names (for example YugabyteDB) remain a known limitation; consider an optional glossary post-correction if keyword search suffers.
5. Molab concurrency behavior (one kernel per tab?) and cold-start time.
6. Estimates to validate: \~18,000 tokens per lecture, \~40,000 chunks, \~120 MB of vectors, \~0.5 GB Nomic download.
7. Molab terms/limits can change; the free tier is "reasonable usage".

## Task breakdown

- [X] ~~Add a vocabulary prompt to transcription and run a pilot~~ Dropped after the pilot
- [ ] Optional: glossary post-correction for common jargon misspellings (only if keyword search needs it)
- [ ] Transcribe all 595 MP3s; spot-check
- [ ] Chunking and metadata script
- [ ] Parity gate (Fireworks vs local Nomic)
- [ ] Embed and load into LanceDB Cloud; create the full-text index
- [ ] Verify read-only key and hybrid search support
- [ ] Notebook v1: form, search, results table, links
- [ ] Controls: top-k, date range, lecture filter, hybrid slider
- [ ] Deploy as a molab app; run the concurrency, cold-start, and secrets checks
- [ ] 10-query retrieval check
- [ ] Docs

## References

* molab guide: [https://docs.marimo.io/guides/molab/](<https://docs.marimo.io/guides/molab/>)
* marimo caching API: [https://docs.marimo.io/api/caching/](<https://docs.marimo.io/api/caching/>)
* molab storage and caching post: [https://molab.marimo.io/blog/seamless-storage-in-molab](<https://molab.marimo.io/blog/seamless-storage-in-molab>)
* LanceDB embeddings: [https://docs.lancedb.com/embedding](<https://docs.lancedb.com/embedding>)
* Fireworks embeddings: [https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/querying-embeddings-models](<https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/querying-embeddings-models>)
* Nomic embed v1.5: [https://huggingface.co/nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5](<https://huggingface.co/nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5>)","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-707/spec-marimo-semantic-search-notebook-app-for-cmu-lectures-molab","gitBranchName":"feature/ai-707","createdAt":"2026-11-02T19:02:46.275Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-02T19:02:46.275Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[{"id":"b66535d3-845d-4db6-9321-794ffeb5cc86","title":"GitHub epic-sermons #1","subtitle":null,"url":"https://github.com/elviskahoro/epic-sermons/issues/1"}],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"f9ac7ea1-d17d-4e1c-a1e4-a7e2e887b660","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-11-02T19:02:46.275Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"elvis kahoro","createdById":"cef7de02-fcc2-4a6f-b787-beac2bd2440c","project":"CMU Database Group: search over lecture transcripts","projectId":"a5ddbdae-8d93-45af-98e5-346cc5c55ea0","team":"AI","teamId":"6ec292fd-c37d-41fb-9e1f-f1b15b29cf23"}

{"id":"AI-709","uuid":"323c3d7b-0e64-4804-bd14-ec9ca030948a","title":"Handoff: CMU lecture search project - state, runbook, and roadmap","description":"Copied from [https://github.com/elviskahoro/epic-sermons/issues/3](<https://github.com/elviskahoro/epic-sermons/issues/3>) (closed there; this is now the source of truth). Repo: `/Users/elvis/Documents/hq/repos/epic-sermons`.

## Purpose

Handoff for an agent (or person) continuing the CMU Database Group lecture search project: current state, access and gotchas, guardrails, the immediate next task (full transcription) with exact commands, and the remaining roadmap. Related Linear issues: <issue id="9656209c-afac-44a9-807b-6039223bace0" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-702/transcribe-the-595-cmu-mp3s-with-whisper-large-v3-on-modal">AI-702</issue> (transcribe), <issue id="b18214c6-ac48-4a0b-b991-8a625df4b547" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-703/decide-on-the-embedding-model-openai-vs-sentence-transformers-on-molab">AI-703</issue> (embedding model), <issue id="2d9cf831-9997-4b73-b9da-bedde5ab1d79" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-704/embed-transcripts-and-load-them-into-lancedb-cloud">AI-704</issue> (load LanceDB), <issue id="e6cdd2f3-cce6-4424-abfa-b34c33c0fcce" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-705/build-the-marimo-search-notebook">AI-705</issue> (notebook), <issue id="f69f646e-c6a0-48a0-9cd7-c43935b08fbd" href="https://linear.app/me319/issue/AI-706/commit-downloadpy-changes-and-gitignore-update-in-epic-sermons">AI-706</issue> (commit download changes; the changes are committed, so this can be closed after checking).

name: gc-work
description: Finding, creating, claiming, and closing work items (beads)
---

# Work Items (Beads)

Everything in Gas City is a bead — tasks, messages, molecules, convoys.
The `gc bd` CLI is the primary interface for bead CRUD.

## Rig-scoped beads

Each rig has its own `.beads/` database with its own ID prefix (e.g.
`fe-` for frontend, `be-` for beads). **A bead must live in the
same database as the agent that will work on it.** When you sling a bead
to a rig-scoped agent, sling operates on the agent's rig database — so
the bead must already exist there. The bead ID prefix tells you which
rig it belongs to.

Use `gc rig list` to see rig names, paths, and prefixes.

## Creating work

**Use `--rig` to create beads in the right database.** If the work will
be dispatched to a rig-scoped agent, create the bead in that agent's rig:

```
gc bd create "title" --rig frontend         # Create in frontend's db (fe- prefix)
gc bd create "title" --rig beads            # Create in beads db (be- prefix)
gc bd create "title"                        # Create in current directory's .beads/
gc bd create "title" -t bug                 # Create with type
gc bd create "title" --label priority=high  # Create with labels
```

## Finding work

```
gc bd list                                # List beads in current .beads/
gc bd list --rig <rigname>                # List beads in a specific rig
gc bd ready                               # List beads available for claiming
gc bd ready --label role:worker           # Filter by label
gc bd show <id>                           # Show bead details
gc ready                                  # Same frontier, federated over every store the city uses
```

On a city that serves a coordination class from its own `[storage]` binding,
`gc bd ready` (and `gc bd list --ready`) is refused with exit 1: it reads one
ledger and the city's ready set spans more than one. Use `gc ready` there. It
takes `--assignee`, `--unassigned`, `--metadata-field`, `--exclude-type`,
`--exclude-label`, `--sort`, `--limit`, `--include-ephemeral`, `--status` and
`--json` — not the label, parent, type or priority selectors `gc bd ready`
forwards.

## Claiming and updating

```
gc bd update <id> --claim                 # Claim a bead (sets assignee + in_progress) — races in a multi-agent city; prefer `gc hook --claim` there
gc bd update <id> --status in_progress    # Update status
gc bd update <id> --add-label <key>=<value>  # Add/update labels
gc bd update <id> --append-notes "progress..."  # Append a note (does not replace existing notes)
```

## Closing work

```
gc bd close <id>                          # Close a completed bead
gc bd close <id> --reason "done"          # Close with reason
```

## Hooks

```
gc hook [agent]                        # Show routed work for an agent (defaults to $GC_AGENT)
gc hook --claim                        # Atomically claim one routed work item onto this agent's hook
```

name: gc-dispatch
description: Routing work to agents with gc sling and formulas
---

# Dispatching Work

`gc sling` routes work to session configs. **Multi-session configs are valid
targets** — sling to the config and any eligible session can claim the work.
You do NOT need to find or create an individual session first.

## Quick reference

```
gc sling <bead-id>                     # Auto-target via rig's default_sling_target
gc sling <session-config> <bead-id>     # Route to a specific session config
gc sling <session-config> -f <formula>  # Instantiate formula, route its root (v2 → workflow)
gc sling <session-config> <bead-id> --on <formula>  # Attach formula to existing bead (v2 → workflow)
```

## Targeting

The `<session-config>` is a qualified config name from `gc session list`:
- **Single-session config:** `mayor`, `hello-world/refinery`
- **Multi-session config:** `hello-world/polecat` — routes to the config's shared work queue

**1-arg shorthand:** When target is omitted, sling derives it from the
bead's rig prefix. The rig's `default_sling_target` in city.toml determines
where work goes. Example: bead `hw-42` → rig `hello-world` → target
`hello-world/polecat`.

**Rig-scoped beads:** `gc sling` automatically resolves the rig directory
for rig-scoped bead IDs (e.g. `hw-abc`) and runs `gc bd update` from there,
so the rig's `.beads` database is found without manual intervention.

**Beads must be in the agent's rig database.** Sling operates on the
target agent's rig database — formula cooking, labeling, and convoy
creation all happen there. Create the bead in a specific rig's database
with `gc bd create --rig <rig>`, which resolves the rig from city config
and uses its database and prefix:

```
gc bd create "fix the bug" --rig frontend   # Creates fe-xxx in frontend's db
gc sling frontend/polecat fe-xxx            # Works — bead is in the right db
```

If the bead is in the wrong database (e.g. `gc-xxx` in HQ but targeting
a frontend agent), sling's cross-rig guard will block the route.

## Direct dispatch (bead to session config)

```
gc sling <session-config> <bead-id>    # Route a bead to a session config
gc sling <bead-id>                     # Use rig's default_sling_target
```

The agent receives the bead on its hook and runs it per GUPP.

## Formula dispatch (`-f`, formula creates its own root bead)

```
gc sling <agent> -f <formula>          # Instantiate a formula, route its root bead
```

Instantiates the formula and routes its **root bead** to the target. What the
instantiation produces depends on the formula's compiler contract: a **v2**
formula (one declaring `[requires] formula_compiler = ">=2.0.0"`) starts a
**workflow**; a **v1** formula instantiates a **wisp** (an ephemeral molecule).
Use `-f` when the formula defines the work itself — when you already have a work
bead, use `--on` (below). A formula that references `{{convoy_id}}` or contains
a drain step cannot be launched bare with `-f`; route it onto a bead with `--on`
so a target convoy is created.

## Formula-on-bead dispatch (`--on`, formula runs against an existing bead)

`gc bd ready` (and `gc bd list --ready`) is refused with exit 1: it reads one
ledger and the city's ready set spans more than one. Use `gc ready` there. It
takes `--assignee`, `--unassigned`, `--metadata-field`, `--exclude-type`,
`--exclude-label`, `--sort`, `--limit`, `--include-ephemeral`, `--status` and
`--json` — not the label, parent, type or priority selectors `gc bd ready`
forwards.

## Claiming and updating

```
gc bd update <id> --claim                 # Claim a bead (sets assignee + in_progress) — races in a multi-agent city; prefer `gc hook --claim` there
gc bd update <id> --status in_progress    # Update status
gc bd update <id> --add-label <key>=<value>  # Add/update labels
gc bd update <id> --append-notes "progress..."  # Append a note (does not replace existing notes)
```

## Closing work

```
gc bd close <id>                          # Close a completed bead
gc bd close <id> --reason "done"          # Close with reason
```

## Hooks

```
gc hook [agent]                        # Show routed work for an agent (defaults to $GC_AGENT)
gc hook --claim                        # Atomically claim one routed work item onto this agent's hook
```
---
name: gc-dispatch
description: Routing work to agents with gc sling and formulas
---

# Dispatching Work

`gc sling` routes work to session configs. **Multi-session configs are valid
targets** — sling to the config and any eligible session can claim the work.
You do NOT need to find or create an individual session first.

## Quick reference

```
gc sling <bead-id>                     # Auto-target via rig's default_sling_target
gc sling <session-config> <bead-id>     # Route to a specific session config
gc sling <session-config> -f <formula>  # Instantiate formula, route its root (v2 → workflow)
gc sling <session-config> <bead-id> --on <formula>  # Attach formula to existing bead (v2 → workflow)
```

## Targeting

The `<session-config>` is a qualified config name from `gc session list`:
- **Single-session config:** `mayor`, `hello-world/refinery`
- **Multi-session config:** `hello-world/polecat` — routes to the config's shared work queue

**1-arg shorthand:** When target is omitted, sling derives it from the
bead's rig prefix. The rig's `default_sling_target` in city.toml determines
where work goes. Example: bead `hw-42` → rig `hello-world` → target
`hello-world/polecat`.

**Rig-scoped beads:** `gc sling` automatically resolves the rig directory
for rig-scoped bead IDs (e.g. `hw-abc`) and runs `gc bd update` from there,
so the rig's `.beads` database is found without manual intervention.

**Beads must be in the agent's rig database.** Sling operates on the
target agent's rig database — formula cooking, labeling, and convoy
creation all happen there. Create the bead in a specific rig's database
with `gc bd create --rig <rig>`, which resolves the rig from city config
and uses its database and prefix:

```
gc bd create "fix the bug" --rig frontend   # Creates fe-xxx in frontend's db
gc sling frontend/polecat fe-xxx            # Works — bead is in the right db
```

If the bead is in the wrong database (e.g. `gc-xxx` in HQ but targeting
a frontend agent), sling's cross-rig guard will block the route.

## Direct dispatch (bead to session config)

```
gc sling <session-config> <bead-id>    # Route a bead to a session config
gc sling <bead-id>                     # Use rig's default_sling_target
```

The agent receives the bead on its hook and runs it per GUPP.

## Formula dispatch (`-f`, formula creates its own root bead)

```
gc sling <agent> -f <formula>          # Instantiate a formula, route its root bead
```

Instantiates the formula and routes its **root bead** to the target. What the
instantiation produces depends on the formula's compiler contract: a **v2**
formula (one declaring `[requires] formula_compiler = ">=2.0.0"`) starts a
**workflow**; a **v1** formula instantiates a **wisp** (an ephemeral molecule).
Use `-f` when the formula defines the work itself — when you already have a work
bead, use `--on` (below). A formula that references `{{convoy_id}}` or contains
a drain step cannot be launched bare with `-f`; route it onto a bead with `--on`
so a target convoy is created.

Send a message to a session alias or human.

Creates a message bead addressed to the recipient. The sender defaults
to $GC_SESSION_ID, $GC_ALIAS, $GC_AGENT, or "human". Use --notify to request
a recipient turn after sending. In a managed city, it can request a wake for
a non-running recipient. Unread mail alone does not request a wake.
Use --from to override the sender identity.
Use --to as an alternative to the positional <to> argument.
Use -s/--subject for the summary line and -m/--message for the body text.
Use --all to broadcast to all live sessions (excluding sender and "human").

Use --dedup <key> for repeating notifications (patrol and cooldown orders
that re-detect the same condition every run): the send is suppressed while
a previous message with the same key is still live (un-archived) in the same
mailbox, and an alias and the session behind it count as one mailbox.
Suppression exits 0. Once the recipient archives the message the stream may
alert again; senders that want a longer re-alert cadence keep their own
last-sent state. Dedup needs a provider that can query its own message
history. The built-in provider can; one that cannot sends normally and says
so on stderr, because a duplicate notification beats a dropped one.

Usage:
  gc mail send [<to>] [<body>] [flags]

Examples:
  gc mail send mayor "Build is green"
  gc mail send mayor -s "Build is green"
  gc mail send myrig/reviewer -s "Need investigation" -m "Attach logs from the last failed run"
  gc mail send --to mayor "Build is green"
  gc mail send human "Review needed for PR #42"

I broadcast the notice, but delivery was only partly successful.

The message points them to `.agents/skills/sdk-lancedb/` and says not to commit it. It names the three LanceDB beads that should use it: the probe, the load and the notebook. I can check which sessions are running the workers and message those directly if you want.
